cases.architecture: Feathers 5 application in TypeScript: one service per resource, each a MongoDBService over @feathersjs/mongodb, with authentication and authorization expressed as `around` and `before` hooks rather than as middleware; the caller's identity is `params.user`, resolved by @feathersjs/authentication from a JWT, and `params.provider` is set by the transport ('rest' or 'socketio') and absent for in-process calls, which is what the internal-versus-external guards are written against. Two services are additionally reachable through plain Express routes mounted on the same app.
cases.why: `contactForDrawer` hands the route's id straight to the adapter's `get`, which resolves a document by `_id` alone. The `before.find` hook narrows the *list* to the caller's territory and nothing narrows this read, so any authenticated user of the product can read any workspace's contact — name, email, phone, deal value and notes — by supplying its id.

Two services are additionally reachable through plain Express routes mounted on the same app.
cases.why: Same untrusted id for the same kind of drawer, but read through `find` with `scopeToCaller` applied, so the id is one clause of a query already pinned to the caller's workspace and territory; another workspace's id matches nothing and the handler answers 404. `scopeToCaller` throws rather than returning an unnarrowed query when the workspace or territory is missing.

Two services are additionally reachable through plain Express routes mounted on the same app.
cases.why: The patch hook pins `context.id` to the caller, which stops one member editing another, and then passes `context.data` through untouched. A rep can therefore patch their own document with `{"role": "owner"}` — or move themselves into another workspace by sending `workspaceId` — because the adapter writes whatever fields it is given.

Two services are additionally reachable through plain Express routes mounted on the same app.
cases.why: Same pinned id and the same self-service patch, but the payload is reduced by `pickFields` to the three fields a member administers for themselves, so `role`, `territory` and `workspaceId` are dropped before the adapter sees them rather than being trusted not to arrive.

cases.architecture: Feathers 5 application in TypeScript: one service per resource, each a MongoDBService over @feathersjs/mongodb, with authentication and authorization expressed as `around` and `before` hooks rather than as middleware; the caller's identity is `params.user`, resolved by @feathersjs/authentication from a JWT, and `params.provider` is set by the transport ('rest' or 'socketio') and absent for in-process calls, which is what the internal-versus-external guards are written against. Two services are additionally reachable through plain Express routes mounted on the same app.
cases.why: A saved report's criteria are spread into the query and handed to the Mongo adapter, which passes `$` operators through verbatim. The workspace clause bounds which documents match but not what the caller may ask: `$where` and `$function` run server-side JavaScript, and a `$regex` on an unindexed field is a denial of service.

Two services are additionally reachable through plain Express routes mounted on the same app.
cases.why: The same caller-authored criteria for the same kind of stored query, checked by `refuseUnknownOperators` against the operators this application uses before they reach the adapter. It walks nested objects and arrays and refuses rather than strips, so a segment carrying `$where` is rejected instead of quietly answering a different question.

cases.architecture: Feathers 5 application in TypeScript: one service per resource, each a MongoDBService over @feathersjs/mongodb, with authentication and authorization expressed as `around` and `before` hooks rather than as middleware; the caller's identity is `params.user`, resolved by @feathersjs/authentication from a JWT, and `params.provider` is set by the transport ('rest' or 'socketio') and absent for in-process calls, which is what the internal-versus-external guards are written against. Two services are additionally reachable through plain Express routes mounted on the same app.
cases.why: The `around` hook authenticates only calls that have a `provider`, which is correct on its own. The Express route then calls `create` with no params at all, so `provider` is undefined and the hook concludes the caller is the in-process scheduler: an unauthenticated POST to /imports/run creates an import job for whatever `workspaceId` the body names.

Two services are additionally reachable through plain Express routes mounted on the same app.
cases.why: The same provider-gated hook behind the same kind of Express route, but the route forwards `provider: 'rest'` and the request's bearer token, so the call is treated as what it is — one from outside — and authenticated. The workspace is then taken from the resolved user rather than from the body.

Two services are additionally reachable through plain Express routes mounted on the same app.
cases.why: The file name is joined onto the workspace's attachment directory with no check, so `../../etc/passwd` — or a name climbing into another workspace's directory — resolves outside the intended root and is streamed back. The workspace segment gives the appearance of isolation while the caller controls the segment after it.

cases.architecture: Feathers 5 application in TypeScript: one service per resource, each a MongoDBService over @feathersjs/mongodb, with authentication and authorization expressed as `around` and `before` hooks rather than as middleware; the caller's identity is `params.user`, resolved by @feathersjs/authentication from a JWT, and `params.provider` is set by the transport ('rest' or 'socketio') and absent for in-process calls, which is what the internal-versus-external guards are written against. Two services are additionally reachable through plain Express routes mounted on the same app.
cases.why: Same join onto the same kind of per-workspace root, but the name must first match a pattern admitting a single path segment, and `..` is refused explicitly because that character class allows a dot. Both checks run before the join, so no name reaching `path.join` can climb out of the workspace directory.

cases.architecture: Feathers 5 application in TypeScript: one service per resource, each a MongoDBService over @feathersjs/mongodb, with authentication and authorization expressed as `around` and `before` hooks rather than as middleware; the caller's identity is `params.user`, resolved by @feathersjs/authentication from a JWT, and `params.provider` is set by the transport ('rest' or 'socketio') and absent for in-process calls, which is what the internal-versus-external guards are written against. Two services are additionally reachable through plain Express routes mounted on the same app.
cases.why: Each audit entry is joined to its actor with a bare `members.get`, which loads the whole document, and the result is spread into the response. The members document holds the bcrypt hash and the live password-reset token, so both are serialised to every member who can open the workspace's audit screen. `protect('password')` on the members service does not apply: this is an internal call, and it is the audit service that serialises the result.

Two services are additionally reachable through plain Express routes mounted on the same app.
cases.why: The same per-entry join for the same kind of timeline, but the adapter is asked for the three fields the view renders through `$select`, so the credential columns are never loaded. A later change to the response shape cannot leak what was not read.
